payload.guidance: Implement the work item this drive rides on, exactly per the scope journaled on the item and the constraints in PRODUCT.md and docs/adr/. TypeScript on Bun, TDD (failing test first), bun test green before you finish. Commit in small commits on the epic branch.
payload.input: Host-materialized directive for role dev (exec=subagent, claude/opus/high): implement item br5phvfw (llm-client) per its journaled scope — OpenAI-compatible chat client, base default https://api.poe.com/v1, POE_API_KEY from .env.local, returns reply text AND token usage (the usage figures feed nahel's token-cost journaling convention). No mocks in tests: a fake OpenAI-compatible HTTP server in-process is the test double per house testing rules (real HTTP, stub vendor). Branch epic/murder-mystery-game.

payload.summary: verified Bun env auto-load: bun 1.3.10 loads .env.local into process.env at normal runtime (NODE_ENV undefined), but NOT under 'bun test' — bun test sets NODE_ENV=test and Bun deliberately skips .env.local in test env. Probe: POE_API_KEY present=true at runtime, present=false under bun test, same cwd. Consequence for br5phvfw: relying on Bun's auto-load alone would make the client silently keyless in any test or NODE_ENV=test context, so config.ts parses .env.local explicitly as a fallback after process.env, rather than trusting the runtime.

live-verified the provider contract against real Poe (read-only GET /v1/models plus two minimal chat calls, ~1.3k tokens total). Findings: (1) Poe lists 343 models with LOWERCASE-HYPHENATED ids (claude-sonnet-4.5, claude-opus-4.8, gpt-5.4, gemini-3.1-pro) — the founding-era guess 'Claude-Sonnet-4.5' is not a listed id, DEFAULT_MODEL corrected to claude-sonnet-4.5. (2) The chat endpoint matches model ids CASE-INSENSITIVELY and echoes back verbatim whatever casing the request sent, so response.model is caller-controlled, not canonical. That is an attribution bug: keying the session ledger on the echoed string splits one model's tokens across two buckets. Fixed — byModel is keyed on usageKeyFor(model) = trim+lowercase, with a regression test. (3) A 4-token reply to a ~7-token prompt reported prompt_tokens=627: Poe injects a substantial system preamble, so any length-based estimate would be off by ~90x. Concrete evidence for PRODUCT.md's 'measured, never estimated'.

scope tension resolved by offering both surfaces. The item's journaled scope says errors must 'return a failure the caller can degrade on rather than throwing into the game loop'; the host's build directive says non-2xx must produce a typed error. Rather than pick one, ChatClient exposes chat() which throws a typed LlmError and tryChat() which returns a discriminated {ok:true,value}|{ok:false,error}. tryChat catches only LlmError and re-throws anything else, so a genuine programmer bug is never swallowed. The game loop is expected to call tryChat and fall back to plain engine text per PRODUCT.md hard constraint 5; game-master (k0n64xb4) should be built against tryChat, not chat.

CHANGE SUMMARY — item br5phvfw (llm-client), run kqrr2q4q, agent:opus-dev

WHAT EXISTS: an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client (ADR-0002), the project's
only LLM transport. POST {base}/chat/completions, Authorization: Bearer, body
{model, messages, ...params}; returns {text, usage, model} where usage is the
response's own {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens} or null when the
provider omits it. A per-client session ledger sums tokens overall and per model
(TOKEN-COUNT attribution v1, resolution 5rwbt08h). No vendor SDK, no dependencies.

  src/llm/errors.ts   LlmError base + Config/Http/Network/Timeout/Protocol
  src/llm/client.ts   ChatClient (chat, tryChat, usage), parseCompletion, parseUsage
  src/llm/index.ts    public surface
  tests/llm/fake-vendor.ts   real in-process Bun.serve OpenAI-compatible vendor
  tests/llm/client.test.ts   21 tests   tests/llm/config.test.ts   8 tests
  package.json / tsconfig.json  minimal Bun+TS scaffolding (created; sibling raced OK)

TESTS: 29 pass / 0 fail / 106 assertions in tests/llm. Full repo suite 61 pass / 0 fail
(engine sibling included). No mocks anywhere: real HTTP over TCP against a stub vendor.

DECISIONS
- chat() throws typed errors; tryChat() returns {ok,...} — satisfies both the item's
  "degrade, don't throw into the game loop" and the directive's "typed error". Game
  master should call tryChat.
- .env.local is parsed explicitly, because bun test (NODE_ENV=test) suppresses Bun's
  auto-load; env wins over file, explicit options win over both.
- Retry: exactly one, on 429/5xx only, after retryBackoffMs. Never on other 4xx,
  never on timeout. Timeout via AbortController, cleared in finally.
- byModel is keyed on the LOWERCASED model id: Poe matches ids case-insensitively and
  echoes the caller's casing back, which would otherwise split one model's ledger.
- DEFAULT_MODEL = claude-sonnet-4.5, verified present in GET /v1/models.

bindings.crit-codex:
codex
The timeout is cleared when response headers arrive, so a stalled body read can hang indefinitely or escape `tryChat()` as an untyped error.
`parseUsage()` accepts invalid or partial usage and fabricates missing counts as zero, silently corrupting the required token ledger.
bindings.crit-agy:
1. Retrying 429 rate limit responses after a fixed `retryBackoffMs` instead of dynamically parsing and respecting the provider's `Retry-After` header risks immediate repeat failures and exacerbated API throttling.
2. Force-loading `.env.local` to circumvent Bun's built-in test environment suppression breaks standard environment isolation, creating a high risk of tests accidentally executing against real, billed APIs if mock configurations are ever omitted.
